## Review verdict — `review:human` cleared by HUMAN CEREMONY

**Decision:** `clear-human` — the `review:human` gate on this PR was removed by the operator, on the explicit
in-conversation instruction quoted verbatim below. This is a **human ceremony** (#2895), **not** an
established-independent agent review: `--answer=accept` is refused on a `review:human` PR by
`decideSetLabel`'s pure core, and `review-pr` carries no route around it.

**Operator instruction (verbatim):** `Clear PR #1726 — accept`

### Panel that actually judged

| lens | seat | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `correctness` | `--lens` seat, tool-bearing | **accept** |
| `security` | pinned `MANDATORY_LENSES[1]`, tool-bearing | **accept** |

Reduced by `derivePanelVerdict` to **`needs-human`** — *"a human gate applies; the loop does not decide this"*
(round 1 of cap 5, outcome `escalated`).

**Earned vs seated (#3335).** The touch-set derives `careLevel: high` (blast-radius + statute, both on
`docs/agent/platform-decisions.md`), earning `correctness`, `security`, `simplicity`,
`standards-conformance` and `claim-accuracy` at 2 jurors/lens over 3 rounds. Two seats ran.
**`simplicity`, `standards-conformance` and `claim-accuracy` were earned and did not sit.** On a
docs-and-backlog diff that shortfall is broadly proportionate — but finding 1 below is itself a
claim-accuracy defect, so it was not costless.

### Read

- Net basis `141cb7a0…86a9df5d`, 4 files, +250/−11.
- Disposition `{ mode: converge, autoLand: false }` — a sensitivity park. The drain pushed no advisory fix.
- Independence: `stamp-lost`.
- **The head moved after the park.** The drain parked at `04739387` (1 commit); the branch now carries a
  second commit `86a9df5d`. This review judged the current head, not the parked one.

### Findings (3) — accepted as-is, none fixed

All three are `impactIfUnfixed: cosmetic`, all `introduced` by this diff and `worseThanBase`. They are
**knowingly landed unfixed** on the operator's instruction; each is real and stands as filed.

1. **`docs/agent/platform-decisions.md:3187` — branch-only identifiers cited without a provenance marker.**
   The new section cites `WE_DISPATCH_KIND` and `dispatchedAgentVerificationReason` as landed precedent;
   both exist only on `origin/lane/mechanical-dispatcher`, not on `main`. `check:standards`' #3026
   provenance lint flags them. The diff's own `backlog/3405` Done-when item 2 documents this, so the caveat
   exists — just not where a reader of the statute will see it.
2. **`backlog/xmjcqwz-…md:12` — 321-word undivided digest** against a 100-word limit, a new
   `check:standards` warning. The same class of gap a sibling commit in this session lineage had just fixed
   elsewhere.
3. **`backlog/3383-…md:366` — the finding-9 correction is no longer independently reproducible.**
   `origin/lane/mechanical-dispatcher-recovered` is already deleted from the remote, so the diff-stat
   evidence the branch-strategy correction rests on (3058 deletions / 147 insertions, the unique-file list)
   cannot be re-checked at source. The text licenses the deletion and cites real-time operator confirmation;
   no artifact was preserved.

**The claim these converge on:** the PR's test plan asserts *"0 errors, 1512 warnings (pre-existing
baseline; no new warnings from this diff)."* The correctness juror measured the true `main` baseline at
**1509**, going to **1512** with the diff applied — **+3 new warnings**. The 1512 figure is right by
coincidence, not by measurement. Independently confirmed here: `check-backlog-item.mjs xmjcqwz` reports the
321-word digest, and `check-statute.mjs` passes 0 errors / 0 warnings with the branch content applied
(anchors and `codifiedIn` links resolve).

### Doctrine content

Not a finding, but recorded: the statute entry says the Fork 2 ruling *"[m]irrors the already-landed
`no-hand-rolling-around-a-missing-operation` rule."* That rule is an **agent-memory** note
(`agent-memory-src/no-hand-rolling-around-a-missing-operation.md`), not a `platform-decisions.md` statute.
The `#3405` card itself says "memory rule"; the statute entry drops the qualifier. Accurate, slightly less
precise.

The doctrine content itself is internally consistent, its anchors resolve, and it is explicit that the
corresponding `guard-bash.mjs` enforcement is branch-only — so no false enforcement guarantee ships.

**Juror spend:** $1.82 (correctness $1.691 / 50 turns / 14.6 min; security $0.131 / 2 turns).
